answer: Distinct-Origin Quorum Pricing. Each identity must submit an independently generated task with a random seed; rewards accrue only when a quorum of submissions cannot be traced to shared origin. Every additional account folded into one controller raises that controller's effective cost per accepted answer, because quorum matching penalizes near-duplicate origin. An attacker running thousands of sybils pays the full compute and diversity overhead for each, and still fails quorum.
